_about: Magazine Spread v1 (trained 5 Oct 2026 from 2 Top-100 refs: r16 Nikhil (rank 3, Hindi podcast) and r30 snippco (rank 7, work-life motivational); ~/reels/style-train/magazine-spread). The talking head laid out like a printed magazine: one brand colour (maroon by default) owns the frame, a tiny spaced-caps header row, a heavy serif hero word over a small sans lead-in, a solid name tag, colour word pages, the speaker framed as a photo on a coloured page, cream editorial pages with a kicker + boxed key word + italic deck, cut-out pictures on a coloured ground, and cool-graded cinematic cutaways. Hard cuts only.

director.style: Magazine Spread: every frame reads like a page of a printed magazine. ONE brand colour (maroon / deep red) owns the reel: name tag box, word pages, page grounds, boxed key words. The speaker carries the reel; the pages are short and frequent. Typography contrast is the hero: a small plain sans lead-in, then ONE heavy serif word.
director.header: watermark.text: a 3-word header row in spaced caps built from the video's own idea, e.g. 'DREAM     SACRIFICE     ACHIEVE' or 'LEARN     BUILD     SCALE' (non-breaking spaces between the words). It stays on for the whole reel. Write it as three words with periods, e.g. 'DREAM. SACRIFICE. ACHIEVE.' (watermark.spread lays them across the top).
director.nametag: A nametag beat from the first frame to ~2.5 s: NAME in caps, title = what they do (one line).
director.captions: captions.heroes: one hero per phrase (never filler). captions.serif: EVERY hero is listed here too, so heroes draw in the italic cream serif (serifItalic). Phrases without a hero stay small. Mixed case.
director.pages: Per 20 s plan 4-5 pages, 0.9-1.8 s each, never two back to back without the speaker: (1) a wordpage on the accent (bg accent) for a short punch line, big: the payoff word; (2) a stack scene bg card (the speaker framed like a photo on the colour page; lead/key/tail = the words said while it is up); (3) a collage scene paper plain, screen false: kicker (2 words, caps), box (THE key word), deck (the rest of the line, italic) + one engraving; (4) a cutout scene ground maroon with one engraving; (5) a slam on the most charged word near the end. (6) 2-3 ground beats per 20 s (needs "matte": true): the speaker CUT OUT on the accent page (omit color = brand accent) or paper "cream", one big spoken word as text behind them (textColor cream on accent, accent on cream), 0.9-1.3 s, in a stretch where the speaker would otherwise sit 3 s+. Stack scenes: bg card with cutout: true and textAbove: true (the speaker cut out on a cream card, the lead + italic serif key above it), keyColor #F1E6CC. Cutaways: colour stills graded teal (saturate(0.8) contrast(1.15) brightness(0.8) sepia(0.3) hue-rotate(150deg)), hard cuts. Card size like the reference: cardW 780, cardH 790, cardTop 630, cutoutScale 0.92.
director.cutaways: 2 image scenes per 20 s, captions: true, 0.9-1.5 s, cool cinematic grade 'sepia(.35) hue-rotate(150deg) saturate(.8) contrast(1.12) brightness(.85)' (the teal look against the maroon). Public domain / CC0 only from stock_fetch.py; pick by meaning (place, people, scale).
director.rhythm: Picture changes about every 2 s (punches, pages, cutaways), hard cuts only. Leave 0.5-1 s on the speaker after the payoff.
director.ground: THE SIGNATURE: the speaker is CUT OUT over the maroon page for nearly the whole reel. Cover every speaker stretch between pages with ground beats (color = brand accent #7A1426, no text), back to back with the pages, so the real room is never seen. Once or twice add one big spoken word as text behind them (textColor #F1E6CC, textSize 320-380). The plate is drawn at 97% from the bottom edge (zoom.base 0.97, originY 100) and punch-ins stay small (1.07) so the whole head stays in frame with room above it.
director.sound: Sound like the reference (r16, demucs + onset analysis 7 Oct): a dark 129 bpm low-end bed (music deep-techno-ambience, closest library match, distance 6.8) about 16 dB under the voice, and ONE soft mid whoosh (1-2 kHz) on each page change, never on captions: whoosh-3 on word pages and ground text, paper-quick on card pages, whoosh-cine on cutaways (image and wordpage scenes take the sound as inSfx; stack and ground as sfx). Speaker ground beats get sfx none.
